reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and around 5 feet 2 inches tall is false. Historical evidence shows that at his autopsy, Napoleon was measured at 5 feet 2 inches in French units (*pieds de Roi*), which converts to approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches (1.69 meters) in modern imperial measure. For an early 19th-century French male, this was average or even slightly above-average height. The myth of his shortness was largely popularized by British propaganda (notably caricaturist James Gillray) and a misunderstanding of the discrepancy between French and British units of measurement.
